target.name: Atomic Industries
target.founder: Aaron Slodov, Austin Bishop, Lou Young Jr

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $25M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $1.8B.

data.narrative:
Atomic Industries is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $25M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 peers across public and private markets, including 8 private companies (Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and others) and 1 public comparable.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy for current value, applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A progression to the $25M base, implying a $50M valuation. Peer-median analysis examines three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B (Series B), Dexterity at $1.6B (Series B), and Walden Robotics at $1.1B (Seed). The median across these three peers is $1.6B, with a range of $1.1B to $1.8B.

The two methods produce a wide triangulated range: $42.5M (low), $850M (median), and $1.9B (high). The substantial spread reflects the disparity between stage-based and peer-based approaches. The stage-progression method anchors conservatively to raised capital; the peer method captures recent valuation expansion in robotics, though peer comparables span adjacent stages (Series B and Seed) rather than precise Series A matches. Key uncertainties include the degree to which Atomic's operational metrics and growth trajectory align with higher-valuation peers, and whether the peer cohort meaningfully reflects frontier-market dynamics versus sector-wide inflation.
